title: CSV parser
blurb: Parse CSV with quoted fields, embedded newlines, escaped quotes and a header mode, with precise errors.
brief: The team needs a small CSV parser with no dependencies. CSV looks simple, but quoting, newlines and blank lines are where hand-rolled parsers go wrong. Implement parseCSV in csv.js. Hidden tests check the exact behavior below, including the error messages.
requirements: parseCSV(text, { delimiter = ',', header = false } = {}). text must be a string, otherwise throw TypeError. delimiter must be a single character other than a double quote, \r or \n, otherwise throw RangeError.
Without header, return an array of records, each an array of strings. Every value is a string: never convert to numbers or booleans.

A record ends at 
 or 
. A single terminator at the very end of the input does not create an extra record. An empty string gives []. A blank line elsewhere is a record with one empty string, [""], so "
" parses as [[""]] and "a

b" as [["a"],[""],["b"]].
Fields are never trimmed. Whitespace inside or around a field is kept exactly.
Empty fields are allowed: "a,,c" has three fields, and a trailing delimiter produces a final empty field.

A field that starts with a double quote is a quoted field. Inside it the delimiter, \n and \r\n are ordinary data (kept exactly as written), and two double quotes in a row mean one literal double quote. The closing quote must be followed by a delimiter, a record end or the end of the input, otherwise throw an Error whose message contains 'Unexpected character after closing quote' and 'line N', where N is the 1-based line of that quote.
A double quote in the middle of an unquoted field is kept as a literal character.
A quoted field that never closes throws an Error whose message contains 'Unterminated quoted field' and 'line N', where N is the 1-based line on which that field started.
A leading byte order mark (\uFEFF) is ignored.

With header: true, the first record holds the field names and the result is an array of objects, one per remaining record. A record with fewer fields than the header gets '' for the missing ones. A record with more throws an Error containing 'Row N', where N is the 1-based number of the data row (the header is not counted). Duplicate names in the header throw an Error containing 'Duplicate header'. Header-only or empty input gives [].
